FN-2564KKK-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 258
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Chris England
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 04/02/2024
REVISED
House Bill 258 as introduced would increase simplified sellers use tax (SSUT) collections by an
estimated $121 million annually, beginning in Fiscal Year 2025, to be distributed 80% to
municipalities ($97 million) and 20% to counties ($24 million), on a pro rata basis, by levying
an additional amount of SSUT at a rate calculated as follows. The average rates listed are the
unweighted averages, as provided by the Alabama Department of Revenue (ADOR).
Tax Tax Rate
General State Sales Tax Rate 4%
PLUS
County General Sales Tax, average 2.39%
PLUS
Municipal General Sales Tax, average 2.94%
LESS
Current SSUT 8%
EQUALS
Difference 1.33%
New Additional Levy (rounded to the nearest tenth) 1.3%
The bill would also provide for ADOR to recalculate this rate every five years, beginning
September 1, 2029.
This bill would only be effective on the passage of House Bill 257, regarding the Alabama
Adventure Awaits Sales Tax Holiday.
Page 1

FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 258
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Representative Chris England
Analyst: Riley Aaron Date: 04/10/2024
House Bill 258 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means Education would levy an
additional amount of simplified sellers use tax (SSUT) at a rate calculated as shown below and
provide for Alabama Department of Revenue to recalculate this rate every five years, beginning
September 1, 2029. The unweighted averages, as provided by the department, are shown below.
Tax Tax Rate
General State Sales Tax Rate 4%
PLUS
County General Sales Tax, average 2.39%
PLUS
Municipal General Sales Tax, average 2.94%
LESS
Current SSUT 8%
EQUALS
Difference 1.33%
New Additional Levy (rounded to the nearest tenth) 1.3%
This bill would increase SSUT collections by an estimated total of $121 million annually,
beginning in Fiscal Year 2025, and would provide for these funds to be distributed as follows:
Receipient Distribution Collections, Est.
Municipalities:
 35% to municipalities with population under 50,000; 65% $79 million
 65% to municipalities with population of 50,000 or more
Counties: pro rata basis 15% $18 million
State Department of Education: to county and municipal
20% $24 million
school boards by average daily membership
This bill would only be effective on the passage of House Bill 257, regarding the Alabama
Adventure Awaits Sales Tax Holiday.
